epistemic_boundary: These records are operator-supplied proposals for criticism and planning. They are not canonical admissions, evidence, runs, results, rankings, confidence statements, or procurement commitments.

origin_story.label: Origin story for volumetric recurrent calculation
origin_story.text: A conjectural path begins with femtosecond-written volumetric waveguides and recurrent optical feedback: if a material can preserve a large addressable state volume while a controlled loop repeatedly applies a calibrated operator, the volume might serve as a recurrent computational medium. This is a design-origin story, not a result, and it remains open until exact state, operator, calibration, and falsifier tests are completed.
nonclaims: The origin story does not claim that any material already performs volumetric recurrent calculation.
It does not claim useful scale, stability, universality, energy efficiency, or a production device.
It does not convert any cited material paper into evidence for the proposed calculation.
It does not claim that recurrence, volumetric storage, and computation are the same property.

items.title: Chiral-nematic typed-junction 2-to-2 interaction-net rewrite

protocols.name: Blind matched-junction drive
protocols.minimal_decisive_test: Prepare the same typed local pair and boundary repeatedly, blind the operator to remote graph context, apply the declared global drive, and test whether the output topology is invariant to remote context.
steps: Prepare and image typed trivalent junctions with a distinguished principal arm.
Randomize remote graph context while holding local pair and boundary labels fixed.
Apply the same non-pair-selective pulse schedule.
Blindly classify the four-boundary output and retain raw image stacks.
protocols.decision_rule: A local rewrite survives this test only if output class and boundary state meet the predeclared tolerance across matched local inputs and remote contexts.
protocols.boundary: The result is limited to the named cell, preparation, pulse schedule, imaging pipeline, and tested finite graph contexts.

controls.expected_relation: No drive should not create the declared rewrite signature.

controls.description: Remote graph context is randomized while local labels remain fixed.
controls.expected_relation: A local mechanism predicts no systematic output dependence on remote context.

calibration.method: calibrated reference grid and independent focus check
calibration.acceptance: scale drift below the predeclared reconstruction tolerance

repetitions.stopping_rule: stop only after all matched blocks or a predeclared safety stop

uncertainty.reporting: publish per-trial labels, excluded trials, and raw image hashes

success_criteria.threshold_text: predeclared tolerance with confidence interval reported descriptively

falsifiers.statement: Output class changes systematically with remote context while local pair and boundary are held fixed.

confounds.confound: unlogged spatial field or tweezer guidance selects reconnection
confounds.detection_control: map fields and retain intervention logs

items.title: Graphene complementary-frequency dense matrix multiplication

protocols.name: Complementary-frequency identity test
protocols.minimal_decisive_test: Encode two finite matrices into complementary optical frequencies, measure the nonlinear mixing output, and compare against an independently computed dense product under randomized phase and amplitude controls.
steps: Calibrate frequency response and detector linearity.
Inject matrix-coded complementary-frequency fields.
Acquire raw complex spectra and decode the candidate product.
Repeat with shuffled, phase-scrambled, and zero-row controls.
protocols.decision_rule: The candidate survives only if decoded entries track the exact reference product within the predeclared error budget and controls reject linear leakage explanations.
protocols.boundary: The test covers only the declared matrix size, frequency band, material stack, and detector reconstruction.

controls.description: Remove the nonlinear interaction region while preserving the readout path.
controls.expected_relation: Dense product signature should disappear or fall below threshold.

observables.name: relative matrix product error
observables.uncertainty_reporting: report detector noise and calibration propagation

calibration.method: traceable power sweep across the operating band
calibration.acceptance: residual linearity error below the product error budget

repetitions.randomization: matrix entries, phases, and order randomized
repetitions.stopping_rule: complete all matrix blocks unless safety or detector saturation stop is reached

uncertainty.sources: laser phase noise, detector noise, frequency drift, nonlinear material variation
uncertainty.propagation: Monte Carlo the calibrated input covariance through decode and norm
uncertainty.reporting: publish matrices, raw spectra, calibration files, and exact oracle output

success_criteria.statement: Decoded output agrees with the exact dense product within the predeclared error budget.

falsifiers.statement: The same product signature remains when the nonlinear interaction is ablated.

confounds.confound: frequency drift masquerades as complementary mixing

raw_artifacts.retention: retain original acquisition and decode code hash

nonclaims: No graphene material performance or scaling is admitted by this fixture.
It does not claim a universal optical matrix processor or useful energy efficiency.
No measurement is a result; this record only specifies a decisive protocol.

equipment_requirements.capability: complex spectral readout with calibrated dynamic range

topic_links.rationale: The topic supplies a bounded optical measurement boundary for the proposed frequency-domain test.

protocols.name: Mode-resolved conservation balance
protocols.minimal_decisive_test: Prepare known input OAM and transverse modes, apply a declared interaction, and compare input and output modal charge and energy balances with phase-resolved readout.
steps: Calibrate mode sorter and phase reference.
Inject randomized known mode tuples.
Acquire complex modal amplitudes before and after interaction.
Compute conserved and leaked modal quantities.
protocols.decision_rule: Conservation survives only if all declared balance residuals stay within the uncertainty interval and mode leakage controls are bounded.
protocols.boundary: Finite mode basis and one interaction geometry only.

controls.expected_relation: No interaction should preserve the calibrated baseline.

uncertainty.reporting: publish residuals and leakage by tuple

items.title: OAM angular collision/interference and contraction variant

protocols.name: Two-mode angular collision and contraction test
protocols.minimal_decisive_test: Collide two independently prepared OAM/multimode wave packets with controlled relative phase and angle, and discriminate a local angular-interference/contraction rule from linear superposition and detector artifacts.
steps: Calibrate angular alignment and phase delay.
Prepare matched positive, negative, and zero-charge mode pairs.
Sweep collision angle and relative phase in blinded order.
Record full far-field and near-field complex readouts and test the declared angular contraction.
protocols.decision_rule: The proposed nonlinear angular rule survives only if its predicted phase/angle dependence and contraction signature beat the linear and no-collision controls within uncertainty.
protocols.boundary: Declared mode pair, geometry, phase range, contraction rule, and detector band.

controls.description: Replace interaction medium with a linear reference path.

repetitions.randomization: phase, angle, and charge-pair order randomized

uncertainty.sources: angle, phase, detector, mode decomposition, and medium drift
uncertainty.propagation: joint fit with calibration nuisance parameters
uncertainty.reporting: report model comparison inputs, not a confidence ranking

success_criteria.statement: The declared angular-interference signature is reproducible and absent from the linear reference.

falsifiers.statement: The signature is fully explained by linear interference, alignment, or detector cross-talk.

confounds.confound: angle-dependent clipping changes the mode basis

raw_artifacts.retention: retain raw frames and phase logs

No collision result, quantum claim, contraction law, or computation claim is admitted.

items.title: Femtosecond-written perovskite/LiNbO3/chalcogenide exact optical computing cell

protocols.name: Finite-state exact operator readout across three material variants
protocols.minimal_decisive_test: Write the same finite optical circuit separately in perovskite, LiNbO3, and chalcogenide variants, inject enumerated basis states, and compare decoded outputs against an exact symbolic oracle with calibrated phase and loss accounting.
steps: Write and inspect matched finite circuits in the perovskite, LiNbO3, and chalcogenide variants.
Calibrate coupling, phase, and detector response for each material variant.
Run all basis states and selected superpositions.
Compare raw complex outputs with the exact oracle and retain variant-specific controls.
protocols.decision_rule: The finite operator is supported only if every declared basis output in each material variant meets the exact oracle tolerance and controls isolate crosstalk.

controls.expected_relation: Output should match the bypass matrix, not the candidate operator.

observables.measurement: complex matrix difference to exact oracle

calibration.acceptance: phase drift below oracle comparison tolerance

repetitions.randomization: basis and circuit section order randomized

uncertainty.reporting: retain raw traces and exact code commit

success_criteria.statement: Decoded finite operator agrees with the exact symbolic oracle within tolerance.

falsifiers.statement: A basis-state output cannot be distinguished from a bypass or crosstalk model at the declared precision.

protocols.name: Volume-addressed state and operator test

steps: Write a finite 3-D address grid.

Run one pass and repeated feedback passes on basis states.
Compare address cross-talk and operator output with a volumetric simulation.

items.title: Adaptive recurrent mixed-halide perovskite operator

targets.target_label: operator-supplied adaptive recurrent mixed-halide perovskite proposal

protocols.name: Closed-loop adaptive operator test
protocols.minimal_decisive_test: Apply a fixed sequence of optical inputs to a mixed-halide perovskite loop while an explicit controller adapts one declared parameter, then distinguish recurrent state adaptation from photochemical drift.
steps: Measure baseline response and halide-state proxy.
Run fixed-input feedback blocks with controller logs.
Repeat with adaptation disabled and randomized input order.
Fit a bounded state-space model to raw traces.
protocols.decision_rule: An adaptive recurrent operator survives only if held-out sequence prediction and state reset tests distinguish it from drift and memoryless controls.

controls.description: Reset optical and thermal state between blocks.
controls.expected_relation: Persistent history dependence must follow the declared state variable.

calibration.method: reference lamp and fixed spectral lines

uncertainty.sources: photochemical drift, thermal drift, spectral calibration, controller latency
uncertainty.propagation: hierarchical block model with reset and adaptation controls
uncertainty.reporting: retain controller logs and raw spectra

success_criteria.statement: The adaptive loop improves held-out sequence prediction beyond disabled and reset controls.

falsifiers.statement: A drift-only model explains the same sequence and state dependence without adaptive updates.

confounds.confound: thermal history is mistaken for adaptive state
confounds.mitigation: include temperature as a measured nuisance variable

raw_artifacts.retention: retain raw sensor, controller, and input streams

nonclaims: No recurrent computing result is claimed.
The fixture does not claim perovskite stability, adaptation mechanism, or useful scale.

items.title: Rust exact oracle and HVM symbolic reduction for amplitudes at infinity

targets.target_label: operator-supplied exact oracle plus HVM symbolic reduction proposal

protocols.name: Finite truncation versus symbolic infinity
protocols.minimal_decisive_test: Enumerate finite amplitude expressions in a Rust exact oracle, reduce the corresponding HVM symbolic terms, and compare normalized limits and failure cases without treating a rewrite trace as a physical result.
steps: Generate typed finite expressions and truncation bounds.
Evaluate exact rational/complex oracle outputs.
Run HVM symbolic reduction with trace retention.
Compare amplitude limits, nontermination, and truncation error classifications.
protocols.decision_rule: The symbolic encoding is adequate only where it agrees with the exact oracle under declared normalization and exposes, rather than hides, divergent or undefined cases.

controls.expected_relation: Both systems expose non-finite or undefined status rather than a finite result.

observables.name: oracle-symbolic delta
observables.uncertainty_reporting: report truncation bounds, not statistical confidence

observables.name: symbolic reduction steps
observables.measurement: HVM trace length and termination status

calibration.acceptance: normalization is identical in oracle and symbolic encoder

repetitions.randomization: seeded expression and reduction order permutations
repetitions.stopping_rule: complete finite expression corpus and declared resource bound

uncertainty.sources: truncation, symbolic timeout, normalization convention, parser/encoder mismatch
uncertainty.propagation: classify exact disagreement by source rather than averaging
uncertainty.reporting: retain source, traces, compiler/tool versions, and all failures

success_criteria.statement: HVM reductions agree with the exact oracle for all terminating declared terms and classify non-finite terms consistently.

falsifiers.statement: The symbolic system returns a finite amplitude where the exact oracle proves divergence or undefined normalization.

confounds.confound: encoder silently changes variable binding or normalization
confounds.mitigation: publish encoder and exact AST hashes

raw_artifacts.format: Rust source, HVM source, JSON trace
raw_artifacts.retention: retain compiler versions and timeout logs

nonclaims: Symbolic agreement is not evidence for amplitudes at infinity in nature.
This fixture does not claim HVM semantics, physical realizability, or a canonical oracle admission.

topic_links.rationale: The exact oracle and symbolic reduction provide a reproducible next test for the formal fragment.
